description: Creates a permanent, public record in the Capital Signal calls ledger: a call or prediction that anyone can read and that cannot be edited or deleted (a correction is a new call with supersedes = the old call_id). The server stamps the time, so a call records only what was said before then. A call is relative: direction 'long' means the tickers (equal-weight) beat the benchmark over horizonDays trading days, 'short' means they lag it; it is scored automatically once the horizon passes (close before the first session it could act on to the close on day horizonDays). thesis holds the reasoning, evidenceDocKeys the filings behind it, and baseRate the base rate behind it (sample, N and hit rate) where one backs it. Returns call_id, created_at, sha256 and the canonical JSON that was hashed; the hash is published at /calls.txt. Suited to explicit user requests to lock, record, timestamp or publish a call. Free.

baseRate.description: The base rate used: its parameters plus N and hit rate / median excess, e.g. {dimension:'director_joins', priorTercile:'top', horizon:250, n:32, beatBenchmarkPct:43.8}.

benchmark.description: CS200EW (default, equal-weight ASX 200 proxy) or 'EW:<industry group>'.

direction.description: long = beats the benchmark; short = lags it.

evidenceDocKeys.description: doc_keys of the filings the call rests on.

horizonDays.description: Trading days to the verdict, 1-750 (60 ~ 3 months, 120 ~ 6, 250 ~ a year).

label.description: Optional author label, e.g. 'newsletter' or an agent run id; the author is the caller's public pseudonym plus this label.

supersedes.description: call_id of the author's earlier call this one corrects.

thesis.description: Why, in the user's words where possible (10-10,000 characters).

tickers.description: 1-20 ASX codes, e.g. ['SVM']; several = an equal-weight basket.
